transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-11-07 15:00 PT
- Duration: 45m
- Attendees: see metadata

Summary (auto): Discussed final MSA/DPA redlines, SLA uptime and SLOs, KMS integration approach, pricing approval timeline. Action items captured.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and DPA exceptions
- SLA details and penalty/credits
- KMS/HSM and BYOK options
- Pricing path for pilot -> enterprise
- Security documentation and evidence (SOC2/ISO)

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Alex Nguyen: Hey everyone, uh good afternoon. Thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this tight, 30 to 45 minutes, focus on the legal redlines and pricing finalization for the pilot. Marisol, over to you for any procurement context?

[00:18] Marisol Reyes: Yeah thanks Alex. Uh hi all, we have a compressed timeline, procurement and finance want a signed DPA+MSA before we spin up any paid usage. Our main asks, um, are BYOK (bring your own key) or a KMS integration, a clear SLA with credits spelled out, and clarity on egress fees — our compliance team flagged that. We also need SOC2 docs and a basic attestation on labor jurisdiction stuff.

[00:42] Alex Nguyen: Totally. Priya and I will walk through how those map to Redwood offerings — hosted vs dedicated vs private — and what we can commit to in the MSA.

[00:51] Priya Menon: Hi all. Quick overview: for BYOK we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations and there's an HSM-backed option for Private deployments. For Hosted we offer a KMS integration layer with envelope encryption, but true key custody on-prem is part of our Private product. I realize there are nuances in the DPA language around key custody that we should clean up.

[01:20] Ethan Li: Right, so the ask from security is we need proof of key separation and that Redwood can't decrypt customer data without the customer key. Also, rotation policy and access logs — we need auditability.

[01:33] Priya Menon: Yep, we can provide key usage logs and rotation metadata. In Private deployments keys remain in customer controlled HSM, so programmatically Redwood can't access plaintext. For Hosted, it's envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS in the customer's cloud account — we never hold unencrypted keys. We'll attach architecture diagram in the security pack.

[01:55] Marisol Reyes: Okay good. On the MSA itself, legal redlined the indemnity and limitation of liability sections. Our counsel is pushing for a stronger data indemnity clause — they want to ensure vendor responsibility if there's downstream leakage.

[02:12] Alex Nguyen: Understood. We typically put liability caps tied to fees paid in 12 months, but for enterprise customers we have flexibility. I can escalate to our legal ops for a middle ground. Could you send those exact redlines?

[02:28] Marisol Reyes: Yes we'll push them in the contract portal after the call.

[02:34] Daniel Cho: From finance — two items: 1) we need the exact pilot pricing and expected spend profile to route to the approver; 2) payment terms, net 30 vs net 45 and any prepay discounts.

[02:48] Alex Nguyen: For the pilot we proposed a time-limited discounted rate — I'll include the line items in the MSA appendix. Net 30 standard, but we can discuss prepay credits if you want to convert pilot to reserved capacity.

[03:01] Priya Kapoor (customer): Quick question on SLA: what are the latency and uptime commitments for hosted? Our apps are latency-sensitive and we need tail-latency percentiles more than average.

[03:13] Priya Menon: Good point. Our hosted SLA is 99.9% regional availability for API endpoints; we can share p95/p99 latency baselines for your model class. Tail latency depends on batching and model selection — for smaller embeddings workloads we've seen 95th around 120ms, 99th around 300–400ms in our benchmarks, but that's workload dependent. We'll run a perf check on your exact dataset.

[03:43] Ethan Li: Are those numbers with caching on? We plan to use prefix caching aggressively. Also, what about automatic fallback to lower-cost quantized models — how does that show up in the SLA and ROI?

[03:55] Priya Menon: Caching helps a lot, those baselines include typical caching scenarios. For fallbacks, we have routing policies that can downgrade model variants when capacity constrained; SLA applies to the API endpoint availability, not necessarily to a specific model variant. If guaranteed model fidelity is required, we can change routing policies in the config.

[04:17] Marisol Reyes: On egress — do you charge for outbound logs and model outputs? Our legal flagged potential variable fees.

[04:25] Alex Nguyen: We bill tokens for inference and embeddings; egress for logs/raw telemetry is typically included up to a threshold, high-volume export can incur fees. We'll clarify the egress thresholds in the pricing appendix.

[04:37] Daniel Cho: Please call that out explicitly — it's a finance blocker.

[04:41] Alex Nguyen: Noted.

[04:45] Priya Menon: Also to add: if you go Dedicated or Private, egress from Redwood-managed networks is minimized; with Private on-prem you control data egress.

[05:02] Ethan Li: Regarding compliance evidence — SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and a pen-test report — can you provide those? We need the latest reports.

[05:11] Alex Nguyen: Yes we can share the current SOC2 report and ISO summary under an NDA. We already have a secured link for customers; I'll include that in the redline package. Pen-test reports are available under a restricted share.

[05:24] Marisol Reyes: Our counsel also wants to see change management and incident response playbooks with SLA for notifications.

[05:32] Luis Ortega: Hi, quick note from CSM: We maintain a runbook and will share incident notification templates; Redwood offers 24/7 incident alerts for customers on enterprise SLAs.

[05:44] Marisol Reyes: Great. Pricing conversation — we proposed a pilot discount but procurement needs to know how pricing scales to reserved capacity. Will there be a committed monthly minimum?

[05:56] Alex Nguyen: There's a standard path: pilot -> reserved capacity (Dedicated) with committed throughput and lower per-token unit. We can model a stepped discount: pilot at X, committed capacity at Y with 20% discount, larger ARR commits get additional concession. We'll send a pricing sheet.

[06:13] Daniel Cho: Also need clarity on overage charges — if we exceed the committed throughput in a month, what's the billing mechanism?

[06:21] Priya Menon: Overage is billed at a negotiated rate per token or per inference unit depending on contract. We'll include example billing scenarios in the appendix so finance can run forecasts.

[06:33] Marisol Reyes: About data residency — we need logs and telemetry retained in-region for EMEA customers. Is region pinning available?

[06:42] Priya Menon: Yes, region pinning is part of the Dedicated/Private offering. For hosted, we can route requests to specific regions and set retention policies, but the level of control is stronger with Private deployments.

[06:55] Ethan Li: One more from security: RBAC and SSO — we use SAML 2.0; need SCIM provisioning and fine-grained role controls.

[07:04] Alex Nguyen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC with roles for developers, auditors, and admins is supported. We'll include a sample RBAC matrix.

[07:14] Priya Menon: For audit logs, we can forward to your SIEM via secure forwarding; retention windows can be adjusted per contract.

[07:23] Marisol Reyes: That helps. On the legal redlines, our legal asked for a rollback clause in case of a data incident that allows us to require a temporary suspend while we investigate.

[07:33] Alex Nguyen: We can accommodate a temporary suspend clause for confirmed incidents with defined timelines for investigation and remediation. We'll propose specific language when we send the redline.

[07:44] Ethan Li: Regarding key rotation — how quickly can keys be rotated without downtime? That's critical for our lifecycle.

[07:52] Priya Menon: With envelope encryption, rotation is seamless from the application standpoint; new tokens will be re-encrypted and KV cache updates handled. There may be a short tail while in-flight requests finish, but no prolonged downtime. For Private HSM, rotation policies are customer controlled so that aligns with your SLAs.

[08:15] Marisol Reyes: Ok, timeline check — procurement needs legal sign-off by 11/20 to hit our deployment target. Is that feasible?

[08:22] Alex Nguyen: We can aim for that. If Redwood legal and your counsel are responsive, 11/20 is reasonable. We'll prioritize the redlines.

[08:29] Marisol Reyes: Final items: would like to run a short 48-hour pilot to validate latency and cost profile before committing. If ok, we'll need an exact test plan and dataset.

[08:40] Priya Menon: We'll prepare a perf plan and a small dataset sample. We'll run it on a hosted instance with the same model family you requested. Also propose a shadow routing to measure production-like behavior.

[08:53] Daniel Cho: For billing during pilot, will you invoice us or provide credits?

[08:59] Alex Nguyen: We can provide a credit for a portion of the pilot and bill the remainder as usage — flexible. We'll spell that out in the pricing appendix.

[09:10] Ethan Li: Quick thing — do you have an allowlist for IP ranges for Dedicated endpoints? We require an IP-based permit for egress from our VPC.

[09:18] Priya Menon: Yes, Dedicated supports static egress IP ranges and we can provide them as part of network onboarding. For Hosted it's more dynamic, but we can discuss maybe peering or VPN.

[09:31] Marisol Reyes: Awesome. Anything else from Redwood?

[09:33] Alex Nguyen: Just to confirm, we'll send redlined MSA+DPA by 11/10, include SOC2/ISO links under NDA, SE will run perf check and share results by 11/14, and security deep dive week of 11/17. Anything else?

[09:49] Marisol Reyes: That covers it. Thank you.

[09:52] Priya Kapoor: Thanks everyone.

[09:54] Alex Nguyen: Great, closing with next steps and action items in the notes. We'll follow up in email and the contract portal.
